content.text: Enter Bertram and the two French Lords.

lines.text: Nay, good my lord, put him to't; let him have his way.
lines.plainText: Nay good my lord put him to't let him have his way

lines.text: If your lordship find him not a hilding, hold me no more in your respect.
lines.plainText: If your lordship find him not a hilding hold me no more in your respect

lines.text: On my life, my lord, a bubble.
lines.plainText: On my life my lord a bubble

lines.text: Do you think I am so far deceived in him?
lines.plainText: Do you think I am so far deceived in him

lines.text: Believe it, my lord, in mine own direct knowledge, without any malice, but to speak of him as my kinsman, he's a most notable coward, an infinite and endless liar, an hourly promise-breaker, the owner of no one good quality worthy your lordship's entertainment.
lines.plainText: Believe it my lord in mine own direct knowledge without any malice but to speak of him as my kinsman he's a most notable coward an infinite and endless liar an hourly promisebreaker the owner of no one good quality worthy your lordship's entertainment

lines.text: It were fit you knew him; lest, reposing too far in his virtue, which he hath not, he might at some great and trusty business, in a main danger fail you.
lines.plainText: It were fit you knew him lest reposing too far in his virtue which he hath not he might at some great and trusty business in a main danger fail you

lines.text: I would I knew in what particular action to try him.
lines.plainText: I would I knew in what particular action to try him

lines.text: None better than to let him fetch off his drum, which you hear him so confidently undertake to do.
lines.plainText: None better than to let him fetch off his drum which you hear him so confidently undertake to do

lines.text: I with a troop of Florentines will suddenly surprise him; such I will have whom I am sure he knows not from the enemy; we will bind and hoodwink him so that he shall suppose no other but that he is carried into the leaguer of the adversaries when we bring him to our own tents. Be but your lordship present at his examination; if he do not for the promise of his life, and in the highest compulsion of base fear, offer to betray you, and deliver all the intelligence in his power against you, and that with the divine forfeit of his soul upon oath, never trust my judgment in anything.
lines.plainText: I with a troop of Florentines will suddenly surprise him such I will have whom I am sure he knows not from the enemy we will bind and hoodwink him so that he shall suppose no other but that he is carried into the leaguer of the adversaries when we bring him to our own tents Be but your lordship present at his examination if he do not for the promise of his life and in the highest compulsion of base fear offer to betray you and deliver all the intelligence in his power against you and that with the divine forfeit of his soul upon oath never trust my judgment in anything

lines.text: O, for the love of laughter, let him fetch his drum; he says he has a stratagem for't. When your lordship sees the bottom of his success in't, and to what metal this counterfeit lump of ore will be melted, if you give him not John Drum's entertainment, your inclining cannot be removed. Here he comes.
lines.plainText: O for the love of laughter let him fetch his drum he says he has a stratagem for't When your lordship sees the bottom of his success in't and to what metal this counterfeit lump of ore will be melted if you give him not John Drum's entertainment your inclining cannot be removed Here he comes

lines.text: O, for the love of laughter, hinder not the honour of his design: let him fetch off his drum in any hand.
lines.plainText: O for the love of laughter hinder not the honour of his design let him fetch off his drum in any hand

lines.text: How now, monsieur! This drum sticks sorely in your disposition.
lines.plainText: How now monsieur This drum sticks sorely in your disposition

lines.text: A pox on 't; let it go; 'tis but a drum.
lines.plainText: A pox on 't let it go 'tis but a drum

lines.text: But a drum! Is't but a drum? A drum so lost! There was excellent command, to charge in with our horse upon our own wings, and to rend our own soldiers.
lines.plainText: But a drum Is't but a drum A drum so lost There was excellent command to charge in with our horse upon our own wings and to rend our own soldiers

lines.text: That was not to be blam'd in the command of the service; it was a disaster of war that Caesar himself could not have prevented, if he had been there to command.
lines.plainText: That was not to be blam'd in the command of the service it was a disaster of war that Caesar himself could not have prevented if he had been there to command

lines.text: Well, we cannot greatly condemn our success: some dishonour we had in the loss of that drum, but it is not to be recovered.
lines.plainText: Well we cannot greatly condemn our success some dishonour we had in the loss of that drum but it is not to be recovered

lines.text: It might have been recovered.
lines.plainText: It might have been recovered

lines.text: It might, but it is not now.
lines.plainText: It might but it is not now

lines.text: It is to be recovered. But that the merit of service is seldom attributed to the true and exact performer, I would have that drum or another, or hic jacet.
lines.plainText: It is to be recovered But that the merit of service is seldom attributed to the true and exact performer I would have that drum or another or hic jacet

lines.text: Why, if you have a stomach, to't, monsieur, if you think your mystery in stratagem can bring this instrument of honour again into his native quarter, be magnanimous in the enterprise, and go on; I will grace the attempt for a worthy exploit; if you speed well in it, the duke shall both speak of it and extend to you what further becomes his greatness, even to the utmost syllable of your worthiness.
lines.plainText: Why if you have a stomach to't monsieur if you think your mystery in stratagem can bring this instrument of honour again into his native quarter be magnanimous in the enterprise and go on I will grace the attempt for a worthy exploit if you speed well in it the duke shall both speak of it and extend to you what further becomes his greatness even to the utmost syllable of your worthiness

lines.text: By the hand of a soldier, I will undertake it.
lines.plainText: By the hand of a soldier I will undertake it

lines.text: But you must not now slumber in it.
lines.plainText: But you must not now slumber in it

lines.text: I'll about it this evening; and I will presently pen down my dilemmas, encourage myself in my certainty, put myself into my mortal preparation; and by midnight look to hear further from me.
lines.plainText: I'll about it this evening and I will presently pen down my dilemmas encourage myself in my certainty put myself into my mortal preparation and by midnight look to hear further from me

lines.text: May I be bold to acquaint his grace you are gone about it?
lines.plainText: May I be bold to acquaint his grace you are gone about it

lines.text: I know not what the success will be, my lord, but the attempt I vow.
lines.plainText: I know not what the success will be my lord but the attempt I vow

lines.text: I know th'art valiant; and to the possibility of thy soldiership, will subscribe for thee. Farewell.
lines.plainText: I know th'art valiant and to the possibility of thy soldiership will subscribe for thee Farewell

lines.text: I love not many words.
lines.plainText: I love not many words

lines.text: No more than a fish loves water. Is not this a strange fellow, my lord, that so confidently seems to undertake this business, which he knows is not to be done; damns himself to do, and dares better be damn'd than to do't.
lines.plainText: No more than a fish loves water Is not this a strange fellow my lord that so confidently seems to undertake this business which he knows is not to be done damns himself to do and dares better be damn'd than to do't

lines.text: You do not know him, my lord, as we do; certain it is that he will steal himself into a man's favour, and for a week escape a great deal of discoveries, but when you find him out, you have him ever after.
lines.plainText: You do not know him my lord as we do certain it is that he will steal himself into a man's favour and for a week escape a great deal of discoveries but when you find him out you have him ever after

lines.text: Why, do you think he will make no deed at all of this, that so seriously he does address himself unto?
lines.plainText: Why do you think he will make no deed at all of this that so seriously he does address himself unto

lines.text: None in the world; but return with an invention, and clap upon you two or three probable lies; but we have almost embossed him; you shall see his fall tonight; for indeed he is not for your lordship's respect.
lines.plainText: None in the world but return with an invention and clap upon you two or three probable lies but we have almost embossed him you shall see his fall tonight for indeed he is not for your lordship's respect

lines.text: We'll make you some sport with the fox ere we case him. He was first smok'd by the old Lord Lafew; when his disguise and he is parted, tell me what a sprat you shall find him; which you shall see this very night.
lines.plainText: We'll make you some sport with the fox ere we case him He was first smok'd by the old Lord Lafew when his disguise and he is parted tell me what a sprat you shall find him which you shall see this very night

lines.text: I must go look my twigs. He shall be caught.
lines.plainText: I must go look my twigs He shall be caught

lines.text: Your brother, he shall go along with me.
lines.plainText: Your brother he shall go along with me

lines.text: As't please your lordship. I'll leave you.
lines.plainText: As't please your lordship I'll leave you

lines.text: Now will I lead you to the house, and show you
lines.plainText: Now will I lead you to the house and show you

lines.text: The lass I spoke of.
lines.plainText: The lass I spoke of

lines.text: But you say she's honest.
lines.plainText: But you say she's honest

lines.text: That's all the fault. I spoke with her but once,
lines.plainText: That's all the fault I spoke with her but once

lines.text: And found her wondrous cold, but I sent to her
lines.plainText: And found her wondrous cold but I sent to her

lines.text: By this same coxcomb that we have i' the wind
lines.plainText: By this same coxcomb that we have i' the wind

lines.text: Tokens and letters which she did re-send,
lines.plainText: Tokens and letters which she did resend

lines.text: And this is all I have done. She's a fair creature;
lines.plainText: And this is all I have done She's a fair creature

lines.text: Will you go see her?
lines.plainText: Will you go see her

lines.text: With all my heart, my lord.
lines.plainText: With all my heart my lord
